records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61 — Concurrent first-time sync requests can both miss findFirst and create duplicate credentials.
records.rationale: The new webhook handler performs a findFirst followed by create/update with no transaction or unique-constraint backstop; two concurrent first-time syncs can both pass the findFirst check and create duplicate credentials for the same (userId, appId). The diff's own comment acknowledges the non-atomic approach ('Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential'), and no DB-level uniqueness is shown. The mechanism is real and verifiable from the diff, though impact depends on concurrency and schema constraints not visible here.

records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Credential-sync fetch responses are treated as HubSpot tokens, causing undefined token fields to be persisted or used.
records.rationale: The diff shows hubspotCalendarService assigns the result of refreshOAuthTokens (which, when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, is a raw fetch `Response` object, not a parsed token) to `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken`, then uses it as a token. The Response lacks token fields like refresh_token/expires_in, so downstream code in the existing implementation would persist undefined fields — a genuine correctness defect introduced by this sync path.

records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — The sync path casts a fetch Response to HubspotToken, persisting/using undefined token fields instead of the endpoint payload.
records.rationale: In refreshOAuthTokens (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts), when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, it returns the raw `fetch` Response object. The hubspot CalendarService diff casts this to `HubspotToken` (`const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`), then proceeds to read fields like refresh_token/access_token from it. A fetch Response has no such token fields, so the sync path would persist/use undefined values — a real defect introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — Accepting `any` and `ZodTypeAny` erases each provider's token contract before credential persistence.
records.rationale: The finding is accurate and grounded: parseRefreshTokenResponse(response: any, schema: z.ZodTypeAny) both accepts `any` and returns the result of schema.safeParse on a ZodTypeAny, so callers (e.g. GoogleCalendarService's `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` before `prisma.credential.update`) lose the per-provider token type and the parsed result's type collapses to a generic safe-parse result. Additionally, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the code substitutes minimumTokenResponseSchema, whose computed keys `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()`

records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no deadline, so an unavailable sync endpoint can indefinitely block OAuth refreshes on request paths.
records.rationale: The diff adds refreshOAuthTokens.ts which calls fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, {...}) with no AbortSignal/timeout. This fetch replaces the direct provider refresh calls on hot paths (Google/Office365/Zoom/Lark CalendarService refreshAccessToken invoked during booking requests), so a hanging sync endpoint would stall token refreshes. This is a specific, grounded robustness/operability concern introduced by the diff, but not a demonstrable correctness defect since behavior is correct when the endpoint responds.
